title: Rabbi Binyamin bar Giddel
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Chullin 125a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.125a.16) he spoke in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. At the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot, chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.1.1.10), he and Rabbi Acha were sitting and disagreeing about the words of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina. In [Jerusalem Talmud Ma’asrot 1:4:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maasrot.1.4.7): “Rabbi Ila reported a teaching in the name of Rabbi Yasa, and Rabbi Binyamin bar Giddel objected.” He is likewise mentioned at the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, chapter 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.9.1.4). Hyman infers from this that he belonged to the fourth generation of Palestinian Amoraim.[^2]

notes.text: The consulted Chullin 125a names Binyamin bar Giddel reporting Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman’s fourth-generation placement remains his inference.

Hyman cites Ma’asrot 1:6, folio 4a. In the linked edition the objection appears at 1:4:7, with the form Binyamin bar Giddul, also found in the linked Terumot. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=762&lang=en) cites the Chullin transmission and the dispute with Rabbi Acha in Yevamot.
